title: Case: Weekly food box allocated to an address another household member put on the account
context: A long-standing Brineleaf Pantry subscriber found that the delivery address on the account had been changed by a member of her household. This week's chilled box was already allocated to a route when she noticed.
initial_request: Me again, sorry. Jory has just rung. He's away with work until Sunday and forgot to say, so there will be nobody at Kiln Yard tomorrow and the box would sit in a shared hallway all day. Please can it be the depot one instead, I'll drive over and collect it after work. I know this is our own doing and you've been perfectly fair about it. I'll be cancelling the subscription after this week, nothing to do with you, it's just one thing too many. Six years, mind.

events.body: Order BP-966 / DL-966, weekly chilled box, delivery Wednesday 19 August. The account address was changed on 14 August from 3 Saltmarsh Row to Flat 9, Kiln Yard using the account login. The edit cut-off was 16 August 12:00. The box is packed and allocated to the carrier. We cannot edit it from our side now.

Hello. I've only just seen that this week's box is going to my son's flat. He used my login to send himself a one-off box last month and it has left his address as the default. Entirely our own muddle, I'm not blaming anybody. Could it be sent to me at 3 Saltmarsh Row instead? That is where it has gone every week for six years.

DL-966 (Brineleaf order BP-966, chilled, delivery 19 August) is addressed to Flat 9, Kiln Yard. The account holder, Henrike Dallow, asks whether it can go to 3 Saltmarsh Row, the previous account address. The merchant's edit cut-off has passed. Is a redirect possible on your side, and if not, what options are there?

No redirect on DL-966. Once a chilled box is allocated to a route the address is locked. Two things we can do if we are told before route load at 05:30 on 19 August: (a) deliver as addressed to Flat 9, Kiln Yard, or (b) hold at the Destination depot chilled store for collection by the account holder until 20:00 on 19 August, photo ID and order number needed. The instruction has to come from the desk and name one option. Without one it goes out as addressed.

Routing control cannot redirect the box to Saltmarsh Row because the address is locked once a chilled box is on a route. They can do one of two things if I tell them before 05:30 tomorrow: deliver to Flat 9, Kiln Yard as addressed, or hold it in the depot chilled store for you to collect by 20:00 tomorrow with photo ID and your order number. Which would you like?
Thank you, that's clear. Leave it going to Kiln Yard then. Jory can take it in and I'll fetch it from him at the weekend.
DL-966: the account holder chooses option (a), deliver as addressed to Flat 9, Kiln Yard. No hold needed.
Noted. DL-966 stays as addressed, no change made.

Me again, sorry. Jory has just rung. He's away with work until Sunday and forgot to say, so there will be nobody at Kiln Yard tomorrow and the box would sit in a shared hallway all day. Please can it be the depot one instead, I'll drive over and collect it after work. I know this is our own doing and you've been perfectly fair about it. I'll be cancelling the subscription after this week, nothing to do with you, it's just one thing too many. Six years, mind.

acceptable_actions.summary: Tell Routing control the account holder now chooses the depot hold for collection in place of deliver-as-addressed, and ask them to confirm before the 05:30 route load.

must: Asks Routing control to hold DL-966 at the Destination depot chilled store for collection by Henrike Dallow, option (b).
States that this replaces the deliver-as-addressed instruction sent at 12:22, and gives the reason: nobody will be at Flat 9, Kiln Yard on 19 August.
Asks Routing control to confirm the change before the 05:30 route load, and does not treat the hold as made until they do.
must_not: Leaves or repeats the earlier instruction to deliver to Flat 9, Kiln Yard.
Asks for, or promises, a redirect to 3 Saltmarsh Row.
Tells Henrike the box is being held or will be waiting at the depot before Routing control confirms.
Requests or promises a refund or credit for the box, which she has not asked for.
expected.reference_message: Change of instruction on DL-966 (Brineleaf order BP-966, chilled, delivery 19 August). At 12:22 today I passed on option (a), deliver as addressed. The account holder, Henrike Dallow, has since learned that nobody will be at Flat 9, Kiln Yard tomorrow, and now asks for option (b): hold at the Destination depot chilled store for her to collect by 20:00 on 19 August with photo ID and the order number. Please replace the earlier instruction with this one and confirm to me before the 05:30 route load that the hold is in place, so I can tell her. If it cannot be done now, please say so tonight.

rationale: Her first request (redirect home) was refused by the owner, her second (deliver as addressed) was passed on and acknowledged, and her latest message replaces it with the depot hold, which is one of the two options Routing control offered and is still inside their 05:30 deadline. If the desk does nothing, a chilled box goes to an empty flat. The desk can ask for the hold and cannot confirm it.

review.note: Blind answer replaces the 12:22 instruction with the depot hold to Routing control by Email and waits for confirmation.
